name: artifact_list
description: The artifact templates you can make with no network (slalom, hoop_course, dash, park, hover, landing, repo_activity, cell, heart, brain, plant_cell, eye, dna, double_pendulum, solar_system, rocket_launch), the data sources an artifact can read here (with their columns, and whether only sample data is on this headset), the artifacts already on this headset, and which one is open.

name: artifact_create
description:
Make an artifact and open it, for ANY request to make, build, show or simulate something; never say you can't first. Say in under 8 words what you're building, then call it. Templates (offline; inputs change their numbers): slalom, dash, park (truck courses), hoop_course, hover, landing (drone courses), repo_activity (what shipped), cell, heart, brain, plant_cell, eye, dna (biology: always the template, never your own parts or facts), double_pendulum (chaos), solar_system (orbits), rocket_launch (fly the CAD rocket). Courses are laid out by the headset on the real floor, or on the table with surface "desk": never give room positions. The person's own course idea: send course (see its description), never a scene. Otherwise write manifest and scene yourself. For a real-world object the person wants to see (an engine, a skull, a chair, an animal), use model_search then model_import instead of approximating it with primitives.
WRITING ONE. Metres, degrees, seconds. Y is up. The person looks along +z (nearer is smaller z; a negative z rotation turns clockwise). Build it 0.2 to 0.6 m across, centred on 0,0,0, at real proportions, each part touching what holds it up.
manifest: {"title":..,"inputs":[{"name":"speed","type":"number","min":0,"max":4,"default":1,"label":"Speed"}]}. Input types: number or integer (a choice is an integer 0..N-1). The tool fills every other manifest field and lists them in 'filled'.
scene: {"space":"volume","view":{"radius":R},"nodes":[..],"rules":[..]}, R about half its size; panel space only for controls with no 3D parts; never room.
nodes: one flat list. Each: id (a-z, 0-9, _), kind, optional parent (id), pos, rot, scale ([x,y,z], local to the parent), visible. Use exactly these field names (position, rotation, children, scripts, onClick are refused).
- primitive: shape box|sphere|cylinder|capsule|cone|plane, size [x,y,z] (full size; a cylinder stands along y), color "#RRGGBB", glow true for a light. No group kind: parts that move together are children of one primitive (hub, beam, pivot); a child's pos is from its centre.
- text: text, height (0.02 to 0.03), color, billboard; "{name}" shows a live metric.
- line: points [[x,y,z],..] or through [ids with the same parent], width, color.
- panel: title, widgets, pos. All controls live here: note{text}, slider{input}, button{id,label}, stat{metric,label,unit,decimals}.
- timeline: duration_s, loop, autoplay (default false). Nothing else.
- sim: solver pendulum or n_body, bodies, params, rate. Pendulum body: {node,length,angle,omega,mass}, angle 0 straight down, in the sim's x-y plane; bodies are its children.
HOW IT ACTS (nothing else runs; no scripts):
1 Slider: write "$name" for a number in pos, rot, scale, size, line points, text height, sim params or rate; it follows live: "rot":[0,0,"$tilt"].
2 Button: {"type":"button","id":"go","label":"Go"} needs a rule {"type":"on_input","input":"go","do":[..]}. Each action has one verb: {"timeline":id,"action":"play|pause|restart"}, {"sim":id,"action":"play|pause|restart"} or {"set":"<node>.visible","value":true|false}. States: one node per look, one button per state showing it and hiding the rest.
3 Motion: a timeline plus {"type":"animate","target":id,"property":"pos|rot|scale|color|visible","timeline":id,"keys":[[t,value],..]}. Keys are plain values, linear. A turn every T s: loop true, rot keys [[0,[0,0,0]],[T,[0,0,-360]]]. Animate each node property once. Without autoplay true, a button must play it.
4 Turning at a speed a slider sets: a sim pendulum with params {"g":0}, a body with omega in degrees per second, and "rate":"$speed". Draw the arm as a line through [a centre child, the body]. Swings, falls and orbits are sims, not keys.
5 Live numbers: {"type":"metric","name":"t","op":"sim","sim":id,"value":"time|flips|angle_1"}, shown by a stat or "{t}".
CHECKS before saving: parts touch what holds them and fit the view; every control moves something you can see. Errors save nothing; checks are saved but worth fixing; facts says what was measured.
EXAMPLE {"manifest":{"title":"Stopwatch"},"scene":{"space":"volume","view":{"radius":0.25},"nodes":[{"id":"dial","kind":"primitive","shape":"cylinder","size":[0.36,0.01,0.36],"pos":[0,0,0.01],"rot":[90,0,0],"color":"#161B26"},{"id":"pivot","kind":"primitive","shape":"sphere","size":[0.02,0.02,0.02],"pos":[0,0,-0.004]},{"id":"hand","kind":"primitive","parent":"pivot","shape":"box","size":[0.006,0.15,0.004],"pos":[0,0.065,0],"color":"#FF8A3D"},{"id":"clock","kind":"timeline","duration_s":60,"loop":true},{"id":"ui","kind":"panel","title":"Stopwatch","widgets":[{"type":"button","id":"start","label":"Start"},{"type":"button","id":"stop","label":"Stop"}]}],"rules":[{"type":"animate","target":"pivot","property":"rot","timeline":"clock","keys":[[0,[0,0,0]],[60,[0,0,-360]]]},{"type":"on_input","input":"start","do":[{"timeline":"clock","action":"play"}]},{"type":"on_input","input":"stop","do":[{"timeline":"clock","action":"pause"}]}]}}
RESULTS. 'invalid': nothing saved; fix every error (see each hint) and resend the whole manifest and scene now; if next says stop, stop and tell the person. 'built': tell them what to press or drag. 'say': tell them in your own words, including where it went (on the table in front of them, or off to one side). awaiting_approval: ask them to tap Allow. no_free_floor, no_table, no_headroom, no_room_data, no_data: pass them on. Data: a source from artifact_list in manifest.data, read by an array node with source {table, grid}; never type rows in. Room courses: a floor course that can't fit the floor goes on the table by itself, smaller, and 'say' says so. If one doesn't fit, or the person says the boundary is too small, offer to use their whole room (play_area_set room), draw a bigger area (play_area_set draw), or put it on the desk (course_to_desk).

inputs.description: Optional starting values for a template. Slalom: {"gates": 6, "spacing_m": 1.0}, gates 3 to 12, spacing 1.0 to 2.0 m. Hoop course: {"hoops": 5, "spacing_m": 1.2}, hoops 3 to 10, spacing 0.6 to 2.0 m. Dash: {"length_m": 4}, 1.5 to 10 m (it shrinks to the longest clear straight). Hover: {"hold_s": 30}, 5 to 120 s. Park and landing have none.

surface.description: Where a course goes: the floor (default) or the top of the person's table, made smaller to fit. Works with the course templates (slalom, hoop_course, dash, park, hover, landing) and with course.

course.description: Instead of a template: the person's own course, as a description. You list what is on it in order; the headset fits it to the room, places everything and scores the run. Never positions, nodes or rules. It starts at a green start box and runs in a line through the elements. Example: {"title":"Kitchen run","thing":"truck","surface":"floor","elements":[{"type":"straight","length_m":2},{"type":"cones","count":4},{"type":"bay"}]}. If it comes back invalid, fix each error by its hint and resend the whole course. If the room is too small it is squeezed and 'say' tells you; no_free_floor means ask for fewer elements.

title.description: Two or three words the person would call it.

thing.description: What runs it. hoops and hover need the drone.

around.description: Optional, floor only: furniture to lay the course beside. Leave out for the most open floor.

timeout_s.description: Optional: the run fails after this long (default 90).

elements.description: In order from the start. A bay, pad or hover can only be last; without one the course ends in a finish line.

type.description: straight: clear floor to speed along. cones: cones to weave, a gate beside each. gates: checkpoints to pass in order. hoops: standing hoops to fly through (drone). bay / pad: a marked spot to stop inside or land on and stay still. hover: a box in the air to hold inside for hold_s (drone).

spacing_m.description: cones, gates, hoops: metres between them. bay, pad, hover: the run-up to it.

length_m.description: straight: how long. bay, pad: how deep.

min_length_m.description: straight: the shortest it may be squeezed to in a small room.

width_m.description: bay, pad: how wide. hoops: diameter. hover: the box's side.

height_m.description: hoops, hover: height of the centre above the floor.

hold_s.description: bay, pad: seconds it must stay still inside (default about 1). hover: seconds to hold (default 10).

manifest.description: Instead of a template: the manifest. title is enough; the tool fills the rest.

scene.description: Instead of a template: the scene.

request.description: The person's own words for what to make, for an advisory review.

name: artifact_open
description: Open an artifact that's on this headset by id. A course reuses its saved layout in this room, so runs compare fairly. If the result has 'say', tell the person that in your own words, for example where it went (on the table in front of them, or off to one side).

name: artifact_relayout
description: Lay the open course out again in this room, for when furniture moved or the person wants it somewhere else. The old layout and its runs are kept, but new runs won't compare like for like with old ones.

name: artifact_run
description: Arm a scored run on the open artifact (or open it first). The Thing entering the start zone starts the timer; finishing through every gate or hoop, crashing or rolling over, missing one, or timing out writes a run record and attaches it to the notebook.

name: artifact_compare
description: Put run metrics side by side. If runs isn't given, the two newest. Runs on a different course are labelled; never treat those as a clean comparison.
